name: phosphorus_availability
description: A reusable phosphorus-availability module. libRoadRunner/Tellurium SBML P-speciation network (phosphate <-> polyphosphate <-> reactive-P with a precipitation/adsorption mineral sink) driven by a dissolved-phosphate supply, the og-03 thermal-gradient pore enrichment, and pore temperature. Emergent: the standing reactive-P pool, reactive-P production vs precipitation loss (net availability), and the precipitated fraction — does reactive P become available before phosphate precipitates? Requires tellurium.

pore_enrichment.description: Thermal-gradient pore enrichment from the og-03 trap (>=1; 1 = open pore / no gradient control)

loss_rate.description: Precipitation / adsorption loss rate k_prec (1/s) — the mineral-sink bottleneck

speciation.doc:
Real libRoadRunner P-speciation network (phosphate <-> polyphosphate <->
reactive-P with a precipitation/adsorption mineral sink). Reads the dissolved
phosphate supply, the thermal-gradient pore enrichment and the pore
temperature; advances the genuine SBML ODE network each tick; and emits the
P-species pools (overwrite — roadrunner is the authority) plus the emergent
reactive-P production / precipitation-loss competition and a P-mass
conservation residual.

_contract.summary: Real libRoadRunner phosphorus-speciation network: is reactive P produced faster than it precipitates/adsorbs, and does a thermal pore co-concentrate P?
_contract.description: A closed Antimony/SBML phosphorus network — condensation of dissolved phosphate to polyphosphate, activation to reactive P, relaxation/hydrolysis, and a reversible precipitation/adsorption mineral sink — integrated every step by the genuine libRoadRunner ODE engine. The thermal-gradient pore enrichment (coupled from og-03) drives the condensation (enr^2) and activation (enr) routes while precipitation is first-order in phosphate, so the enrichment decides whether phosphate becomes reactive (useful) or precipitates (lost). Emits the P pools, the reactive-P production vs precipitation-loss fluxes, the net availability, the precipitated fraction and a P-mass residual, all as overwrite sensors.

inputs.pore_enrichment: thermal-gradient pore enrichment factor from the og-03 trap (dimensionless, >=1; 1 = open pore / no gradient)
inputs.temperature: mean pore temperature (kelvin) — Arrhenius factor on condensation + activation

outputs.net_reactive_P: reactive-P production - precipitation loss (mole/second); >0 = reactive P wins the race

math: net_reactive_P = Ract - Rprec ; precipitated_fraction = mineralP / total_P
assumptions: Closed P-atom-conserving network (total P fixed by the supply), integrated as an ODE CSTR-less batch.
Condensation is steeply concentration-dependent (enr^2) — the thermal pore makes two phosphates meet; activation scales with enr.
Precipitation/adsorption is first-order in dissolved phosphate with slow desorption (a finite, reversible mineral sink).

emitter.doc:
Store historical states in memory.

``subsample`` records only every Nth composite tick (default 1 =
every tick). Use this for long runs or composites with heavy
state (large fields, many agents) to keep RAM bounded — the
saved time-series still reflects the simulation's true cadence
via each row's ``global_time`` field.

``max_len`` optionally bounds ``history`` to the most recent N
recorded rows (a ring buffer): once the cap is reached each new
record drops the oldest. Default ``None`` = unbounded (the
historical behaviour — consumers such as v2ecoli that read the
full ``history`` are unaffected unless they opt in). ``max_len``
counts *recorded* rows (i.e. post-``subsample``).
